title: Mitkä: selecting several things
focus: Mitkä selects several identifiable things from a group: Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? — Nämä kirjat ovat uusia.
prerequisiteSkills: Mikä: identifying or choosing one thing

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Which books are new?”
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. Mitkä selects several identifiable things from a group: Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? (“Which books are new?”). The accompanying noun takes its plural basic form. The complete question means “Which books are new”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question modifier (asks which item or group) + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state) + description of what the subject is like

parts.role: question modifier (asks which item or group)
parts.formation: Mitkä is the plural basic form of mikä, selecting several identifiable things.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.

parts.role: description of what the subject is like
parts.formation: Uusi has the taught plural partitive uusia.
